text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] elevated model warmup failures in region us-west-2 (warmup error rate 68%). Symptoms: OOM at load, deserialization EOF, JIT compile timeouts, and sporadic CUDA resets. Incident ID: I-20260314-5555

samir: paging oncall. noticed spike around 2026-03-14T16:02 UTC during model rev r13 rollout. warmup workers spiked to 6 per node.

megan: logs show three simultaneous failure modes:
1) deserialization EOF when reading artifact blobs
2) compile-timeout in kernel jitting (timeout 40s)
3) gpu-side process killed after CUDA error 719 (driver reset)
example: 
```
16:02:11Z error deserialize: EOF while reading weights shard (expected 52428800, got 41234567)
16:02:12Z warn jittime: kernel compile exceeded timeout=40s, aborting
16:02:13Z error gpu: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN (719) - process 11023 terminated
16:02:13Z error warmup: OOM allocating 14.7GiB for KV cache
```

eva-oncall: I'm oncall, taking triage. immediate actions: freeze rollout, lower warmup concurrency, divert live traffic away from r13 to last stable (r12). anybody object?

jia-platform: agree. also suspect proxy cache (artifact proxy) is serving partial files under heavy load. will check checksums & CDN logs.

ricardo-ml: model artifact size increased after new quantization layout in r13. combined with aggressive prewarm and small driver headroom, leads to memory pressure. adding deserialization retry is doable quick fix.

megan: executing mitigation commands:
- pause deployment: `kubectl -n inference rollout pause deploy/model-r13`
- set prewarm: `api-client models set r13 --prewarm=false`
- throttle warmup: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/warmup WORKER_LIMIT=1`
Applying now.

infra-bot: Deployment model-r13 paused by megan at 16:06 UTC. Warmup env updated.

customer-success: got a support ping from BetaRetail reporting intermittent 502s and slower chat latency starting ~16:03. tagging them as impacted.

samir: quick metrics: 5xx rate for impacted model peaked at 1.6% cluster-wide. p99 latency for affected tenants jumped to 2.4s. Dedicated customers mostly routed to stable variant; some saw backpressure.

eva-oncall: infra steps planned: 1) cordon+drain suspicious nodes 2) restart inference pods gracefully 3) increase GPU driver memory headroom env 4) roll artifact proxy patch to validate checksums and fallback to origin on mismatch. Jia please execute.

jia-platform: starting node drain on pool-usw2-a, will stagger to avoid mass warmups. also collecting dmesg & nvidia-smi logs for nodes with driver resets.

megan: increasing compile timeout for warmup path to 90s to avoid spurious JIT timeouts: `set-config compile_timeout=90s --scope=warmup`

ricardo-ml: pushing quick deserialization wrapper to r13 canary (catch EOF -> retry with backoff x3). also adding telemetry to count truncated artifact pulls.

jia-platform: artifact proxy grep shows ~2.1% partial fetches from cache edge between 15:58-16:05. pushing proxy fix (checksum verification + retry) to canary now.

ops-lead: need customer impact summary for SEV classification. what's the current impact list and expected duration?

samir: impacted tenants identified: BetaRetail (reported 502s), AcmeCorp (p99 spikes, some 5xx), two smaller tenants saw increased latency only. estimate mitigation to stabilize in 30-45m.

customer-success: sending initial comms to impacted customers noting degraded performance and mitigation steps. will provide update in 30m.

eva-oncall: note: some OOMs are from stale pods that started warmup prior to the throttle change. we'll let them terminate and ensure new pods honor WORKER_LIMIT=1.

infra-bot: Node usw2-n03 reported GPU DRIVER RESET at 16:07 UTC, kernel OOPS recorded. Marking node for deeper investigation.

jia-platform: upgraded driver to 535.37 on two canary nodes; restarted inference pods. warmup smoke test with WORKER_LIMIT=1 passes for r13 artifact fetch + load. compile_timeout increase seems to prevent JIT aborts in the smoke runs.

megan: observed warmup success rate improve from 32%->87% after these mitigations in canary. still watching for truncated artifact counts.

ricardo-ml: checksum guard in artifact fetcher confirmed 0 truncated pulls in canary after patch. telemetry shows 40 partial pulls before patch window. will promote patch to prod after 15m of stability.

ops-lead: setting incident severity to SEV-3 due to limited but customer-visible latency/5xx. schedule 1-hour follow-up and a postmortem within 48h.

eva-oncall: handing lead to jia-platform for ongoing node investigation and artifact rollout. I'll remain reachable for 30m.

jia-platform: taking lead. plan: 1) roll artifact proxy fix to prod (after extra 15m of canary stability) 2) rotate nodes flagged for kernel OOPS to a different pool and perform hardware checks 3) keep r13 prewarm disabled until we validate artifacts end-to-end 4) gradually resume canary with WORKER_LIMIT=1 and compile_timeout=90s.

customer-success: update sent at 16:30 UTC. BetaRetail acknowledged; AcmeCorp requested telemetry logs which we provided.

samir: collecting timeline & logs for postmortem. action items: artifact proxy checksums (jia), deserialization retry & telemetry (ricardo), warmup guardrails (megan), node hardware investigation (jia + infra).

incident-bot: incident I-20260314-5555 status: mitigated->monitoring. roles: lead=jia-platform, scribe=samir, comms=customer-success.

last messages:

jia-platform (16:45 UTC): Promoted proxy fix to prod after 20m stable in canary. Monitoring truncated pulls; initial prod rollout shows drop to 0.2% partial pulls.

megan (16:50 UTC): Warmup success steady at ~95% under WORKER_LIMIT=1. p99 latency returning to baseline slowly.

ops-lead (16:55 UTC): Good containment. schedule postmortem tomorrow. recommend follow-ups: automatic fallback to previous model on 3 consecutive deserialization errors, and pre-deploy artifact checksum verification in CI pipeline.

[thread closed]
